newsitem.title: USA: Telident sees cost benefits in fiscal Q4.
newsitem.headline: Telident sees cost benefits in fiscal Q4.

text.p: Telident Inc said Wednesday that a program to cut its expenses should begin to have an impact in its fiscal fourth quarter.
It reported a loss for the third quarter ended March 31 of $0.25 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.14.

Third quarter sales dropped to $14,950 from $348,437, which the company said was due to a lack of focus on generating new business. Telident said it was expecting a Federal Communications Commission mandate for enhanced 911 emergency telephone response systems which did not occur.
The company said earlier this year it would cut personnel and reduce other costs because of lower-than-expected sales.
"We believe we can achieve profitability and sales growth by more aggressively capitalizing on our current business opportunities," W. Edward McConaghay, president, said in a statement.
The company said it plans $1.2 million in annual cost savings including a 35 percent workforce reduction. It is also trying to reduce accounts receivables and improve working capital.
"Along with our restructuring actions and projected sales levels, we believe we can meet our operating cash needs over the next 12 months," McConaghay said.
Telident is also exploring ways to manage its debt to debenture holders. Measures could include refinancing, restructuring, or conversion of debentures and preferred stock holdings, it said.
Telident designs, makes and markets hardware and software systems for providing the exact location of a 911 emergency telephone call.
